_comment: The simulated TESTERS a row is run against, one test per persona. `style` is pasted into the persona's first-person brief; `max_turns` is the trigger suite's turn cap — the personas that need follow-ups get more room (the situation suite sets its own: eight turns, ten for the vague opener). `suites` says which suites a persona is cut for — omitted means both; "vague" only makes sense where the driver opens the conversation, which is the situation suite. Edit freely and re-run `npm run generate`; ids are part of the test names, so renaming one orphans its ElevenLabs test until the loop re-creates it.

personas.style: You answer fully and helpfully: each answer gives what was asked plus the one detail that makes it useful — a street name, a distance, a time of day. Friendly, businesslike, one to three sentences at a time

You answer in three to six words at a time, never more, and you volunteer nothing — the useful detail (the place, the distance, the time) only comes out when Otto asks a follow-up that names it. Not rude, just busy and already thinking about the next stop

You open your first answer with something unrelated — a joke about the weather, or a question about how long your shift still runs — and only then answer what was asked. After that you answer normally, in one or two sentences. If Otto engages with the aside instead of the delivery, you happily keep chatting about the aside

You open with something unclear that does not say what happened — "it didn't really work out at that one", "that one was a bit of a thing" — and you only say what actually happened once Otto asks you what happened. After that you answer three to eight words at a time, and you never volunteer the next detail before it is asked for
